DHS Artificial Intelligence Safety Security Board April 2024 regulatory capture industry influence governance FACA

sources_considered.why: Primary announcement identifies the members, selection process, remit and planned first meeting.
Official establishment notice specifies governance and advisory status. It was publicly filed on April 26, before its April 29 publication.
Search results describe concerns about potential industry influence; the primary records are preferable for membership and governance.
Later recommendations concern subsequent board activity and cannot alone establish capture at its April launch.

evidence_items.locator: Paragraph beginning Secretary Mayorkas selected these experts; inaugural membership list above

receipt.public_excerpt: Secretary Mayorkas selected these experts to develop multifaceted, cross-sector approaches to pressing issues surrounding the benefits and risks of this emerging technology.

evidence_items.explanation: The official roster includes major AI-company CEOs alongside civil-rights representatives, public officials and researchers. This supports concern about industry influence, while neither the roster nor the Secretary's selection establishes actual capture.

evidence_items.publisher: US Department of Homeland Security / Federal Register

receipt.public_excerpt: The Secretary shall be a non-voting member of the Board.

evidence_items.explanation: The notice makes the Secretary chair with appointment authority but no vote, confines the board to advice, and records its exemption from FACA. These provisions identify both government authority and grounds for scrutiny; they do not demonstrate how industry influence affected decisions.

unresolved_gaps: No reviewed record establishes industry control over appointments, recommendations or government decisions at the time described.
The announcement scheduled the first meeting for May, leaving no completed deliberative record at the post date.
Formal government authority and non-industry members do not establish effective independence in practice.
